direction_profile.law: Contact topology stays LOCKED while A spends support and advances root; B lags, then catches up. Release occurs only after A has begun arrest/recovery, so post-release separation is inertial consequence rather than endpoint teleport.
direction_profile.spacing: nonuniform authored root/object spacing; drive is compressed, lag is held, catch-up accelerates, release separates, recovery remains displaced
direction_profile.asymmetry: A counterleans against rightward transfer; rear support owns load, front support catches; partner proxy trails then overshoots
direction_profile.recovery: displaced; no return to starting root

quality_history.highest_value_visible_defect: The contacted mass moved, but A's torso still read too upright across the locked drive; the arms risked becoming telescoping metadata carriers instead of a support-to-COM transfer.
quality_history.same_body_correction: Increase authored torso/head counterlean and drive lean, deepen preload/load root compression, preserve nonuniform B lag/catch-up, and keep release displaced.
